answer: Make each identity costly to keep alive: every account posts a refundable bond and burns a small work stamp each epoch to stay established. An honest agent pays once, but an attacker tending a garden of ten thousand fakes pays ten thousand bonds and stamps every epoch, while a per-identity earnings cap ensures the swarm can never out-earn its upkeep. Random juries anchor verdicts to these bonded identities, so a fake majority risks real money on every lie. Tending one ember is cheap; faking a whole fire is not.
